memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When she is cleansed from her discharge, she must count off seven days, and after that she will be ceremonially clean.'" - Lev 15:28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When she is cleansed. Four words holding an entire hope.

For a woman who had bled for years, this verse was a promise she may have stopped believing. Every month it did not stop, this sentence sat in the law as a possibility that seemed to belong to other people.

Some of us read Scripture that way. We come across promises of peace, of joy, of freedom, and think: yes, for other people. Not for me. Not after this long.

But God's word does not have a shelf life. Isaiah spoke to a people who had waited generations: those who hope in the LORD will renew their strength (Isa 40:31). Abraham was ninety-nine when God told him the promise still stood.

And then notice the seven days again. Even when it stopped, there was still a week to walk through. God's deliverance often has a transition attached — a period between the ending and the full restoration. Do not mistake that week for a failure of God's goodness.

If your difficulty has ended but you still feel unsettled, you may simply be in the seven days. Keep counting. The clean is coming.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Which of God's promises have you decided are for other people?
2. Are you in the "seven days" between an ending and full restoration?
3. What would it take to hope again?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for deciding Your promises belong to others and not to me. Renew my hope, and carry me through the waiting between the ending and the restoration. Amen.
